subject: chip dipped in salsa
title: What If Everyone Double-Dipped Their Chips?

scenes.text: What if everyone at the party double-dipped? One dip got hit harder than the others.
Scientists at Clemson University tested it. Before any dipping, the dips had no detectable bacteria.
Each bitten chip carried mouth bacteria back in. Three to six double dips moved about ten thousand bacteria.
Runny salsa picked up the most, about five times more than thick cheese dip or chocolate.
Why? Thick dips cling to the chip. Runny salsa drips straight back into the bowl.
But two hours later, salsa had caught up with the others. Its acid kills bacteria. The scientist's verdict: it's like kissing everyone at the table.

description:
What if everyone double-dipped? Clemson University food scientist Paul Dawson found three to six double dips transferred about 10,000 bacteria to the remaining dip, with runny salsa picking up about five times more than cheese or chocolate dip at first.
After two hours, salsa's acidity had brought its count down to the others' level.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Most mouth bacteria are harmless, so the scientist's rule was simple: if you're sick, don't double-dip. Do you call people out for double-dipping?
